title: The Life Divine
author: Sri Aurobindo
description: The Life Divine by Sri Aurobindo (1872-1950), the Indian revolutionary turned yogi, philosopher and founder of Integral Yoga, here in the Sri Aurobindo Ashram edition of the Complete Works (2005). First serialised in the journal Arya between 1914 and 1919 and revised into its final form in 1939-40, it is his principal metaphysical work. Book One sets out the omnipresent Reality as Sachchidananda (existence, consciousness, bliss) and the descent of Spirit into Matter through Supermind, Overmind and Mind, criticising both materialism and world-denying ascetic monism. Book Two describes the ignorance, knowledge and the evolution of consciousness, the triple transformation (psychic, spiritual and supramental), and the emergence of a 'gnostic being' and a divine life on earth, culminating in the chapters on the gnostic being and the divine life. A major synthesis of Vedanta and evolutionary thought, it ranks among the most important spiritual philosophies of the twentieth century.
